what: E94 election-eve forecast and spending nowcast for 2026-11-03, freeze v2 (corrected), frozen before any results. Computed by tools/e94_freeze_v2.py, which runs the notebook's code (notebook_src/examples/E94_midterms_polls_money.py, sections 1-6) on the inputs below.
why_v2: In v1, 2026 nominees with no FEC ID found by name (50 R, 11 D, among them Ashley Hinson, IA-S, filed by the FEC as 'ARENHOLZ, ASHLEY HINSON') had $0 receipts, which pinned their races' money signal at the clip and moved them by about 12 points (IA-S P(D) 0.87 at R+1 in the polls). v2: IDs matched against the FEC candidate master by state, office, district and name (D 100%, R 99.6% found); the money of the 2 still unmatched is missing and imputed; the candidate and IE parts of the spending nowcast use separate random streams; the IE part's uncertainty is included.
information_cutoff: 2026-11-02 (polls ending, reports and IE received, Wikipedia revisions on or before this date)
seats_note: House: D seats incl. uncontested; P_D_control = P(D >= 218). Senate: D-caucus seats incl. 34 not up (32 D + 2 I); D_seats_up counts only the 35 seats up; P_D_control = P(>= 51), VP Vance breaks ties. N = national House two-party margin, D minus R, points.
spending_note: Dollars. Candidates = general-election D and R nominees' committees: disbursements in reports received by 2026-11-02 plus modelled late spending to the 30G coverage end (2026-11-23). IE = general-election independent expenditures received by the eve, plus lag completion and an election-day share, with posterior and cycle-shift uncertainty.
